title: The Hollow Hollow Revisited
premise: Ulyana Dunmore, a cartographer who maps realms that exist only in memory, has spent his life in the Hollow Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow and the gifted hide in plain sight. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive with a list of names, Ulyana learns the valley itself is a dead country erased from every map but his own—and that his cartography is the only key to its last remaining door. Guided by a disgraced huntress who remembers the valley differently than he does, he must reconcile two conflicting memories of home to draw the door into being. In the end, Ulyana opens the way out at the cost of his own memories of the valley, choosing justice for the hunted over the self he was.
about_author: Ulyana Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer appear on any modern atlas. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, legal, and remembered—from a farmhouse full of drawers nobody else is allowed to open.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana works by lamplight on a map of a country he's never seen, while below his window the crown criers announce the gift-hunt. His neighbor is taken that night; her name was already on the hunters' list. The emotional beat is dread curdling into guilt—he always believed invisibility was safety, and now it feels like complicity.

chapters.title: Two Memories of One Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ulyana and Sera Voss, a defected huntress who grew up in the valley before it was 'unmade.' She claims the door stands in the millpond; his maps insist it's under the chapel. Their conflicting memories begin physically reshaping the landscape around them. The beat is uneasy alliance: neither can trust the other's past, but both need the same exit.

chapters.title: What the Crown Cannot Map
chapters.summary: Sera's POV leads as hunters close in and the valley itself begins unraveling—streets looping, names fading from signs—because a country exists only while someone remembers it truly. Ulyana realizes the crown didn't erase the valley; the valley erased itself to survive, and his gift is the thread holding it together. Climax: cornered in the collapsing chapel, he must choose which memory of home is true enough to open the door.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Price
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He draws the door using Sera's memory instead of his own, sacrificing every recollection of the valley—the faces, the lamplight, the reason he hid—to carry the others through. They emerge into a living country that has never heard of him. Resolution: bittersweet freedom; Ulyana begins a new map, blank, with Sera beside him, justice owed rather than given.
